policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV imperative 'Rise' does not distinguish the spelling forms Ἔγειρε and Ἔγειραι; retain the base fallback.
ASV 'without' can render either ἔξωθεν or ἔξω; retain the base fallback.
ASV's idiomatic number 'forty and two' does not securely distinguish absence, addition, or spelling-plus-addition of καί; retain the base fallback.
ASV 'clothed in sackcloth' does not expose the participle's nominative-versus-accusative case; retain the base fallback.
ASV 'standing' does not expose the participle's masculine-versus-feminine agreement; retain the base fallback.

ASV 'shall desire to hurt them' supports the aorist subjunctive shared by the base and reordered r01, but cannot distinguish their word order; it excludes present θέλει in r02, so retain the base fallback.
ASV 'the power to shut the heaven' explicitly reflects both articles and the construction of the base reading; r01 omits the article before 'power'.
The readings differ only in the order of 'with every plague' and 'as often as they shall desire'; ASV word order cannot identify the Greek order.
ASV begins the verse 'And from among the peoples,' directly representing initial καί; r01 omits it.
ASV present 'suffer not' supports present ἀφίουσιν rather than future ἀφήσουσιν.
ASV present 'make merry' supports present εὐφραίνονται rather than future εὐφρανθήσονται.
ASV 'shall send gifts' directly supports πέμψουσιν and excludes 'shall give' δώσουσιν.
ASV 'entered into them' can render either ἐν αὐτοῖς or εἰς αὐτούς; retain the base fallback.
ASV 'fear fell upon them' can render either ἐπέπεσεν or ἔπεσεν followed by ἐπί; retain the base fallback.
ASV plural 'they heard' supports ἤκουσαν rather than singular ἤκουσα.
ASV 'heard a great voice' does not expose the voice phrase's genitive-versus-accusative case; retain the base fallback.
ASV 'voice ... saying' does not expose the participle's genitive-versus-accusative agreement; retain the base fallback.
The direct command 'Come up hither' supports imperative Ἀνάβατε rather than subjunctive Ἀνάβητε.
ASV 'in that hour' directly supports ὥρᾳ and excludes 'day' ἡμέρᾳ.
Both readings contain 'behold, the third Woe' and differ only in Greek order; ASV order is not decisive, so retain the base fallback.
ASV 'voices ... and they said' does not expose masculine-versus-feminine participial agreement; retain the base fallback.
ASV 'who sit before God' can render either the base participle or r01's relative clause; it excludes r02's added 'throne of God' wording, so retain the base fallback.
ASV apposition 'the small and the great' does not expose accusative-versus-dative case; retain the base fallback.
ASV 'the temple of God' explicitly reflects article ὁ; r01 omits it.
ASV 'his covenant' directly supports αὐτοῦ and excludes 'of the Lord' τοῦ κυρίου.
ASV explicitly includes 'and an earthquake,' supporting καὶ σεισμός; r01 omits both words.
